Investigation 5 is complete. The fractional construction is now explicit, although the full no-conjugate-point theorem for every \(0<\omega<\tfrac12\) remains open.

The principal new identities are

\[
a_\omega(t)
=\sum_{n\ge0}
\frac{2(1-\omega)_n}{\Gamma(\omega)n!}
e^{-(1/2-\omega+2n)t},
\]

giving a positive infinite-dimensional diffusive realization, and the complementary Sonine relation

\[
a_\omega*b_\omega
=2e^{-(1/2-\omega)t}.
\]

Consequently, the complementary transform eliminates the fractional sector exactly:

\[
F_{1-\omega}(p+1)K_\omega(p)
=
\frac{2\pi^\omega(p-\frac12-\omega)}
{(p+\frac12+\omega)(p-\frac12+\omega)}.
\]

This reduces the fractional dynamics to a two-state rational boundary system. Truncating the positive mode ladder produces canonical \((N+2)\)-state Riccati factors whose transfers converge to the full fractional system. Passing the factors themselves to the limit now requires a uniform no-conjugate-point estimate.

The strongest progress on that estimate is

\[
\lim_{\omega\downarrow0}
\frac1\omega
\langle f,(I-\varepsilon H_{\omega,L})f\rangle
=
Q_W(\widetilde f),
\qquad R_Lf=\varepsilon f.
\]

Thus the infinitesimal defect is exactly the prime-free Weil quadratic form. Compact-window Weil positivity therefore excludes infinitesimal conjugate directions on \(L\le\log2\). This connects the Riccati bulk directly to the Weil/Sonin-space program developed by [Connes–Consani](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13771) and [Suzuki](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09096).

The remaining small-\(\omega\) proof is a Mosco-convergence problem rather than ordinary perturbation theory. The required next lemma is a uniform logarithmic coercivity estimate preventing minimizing sequences from escaping to high frequencies. The Sonine closure can be placed in [Luchko’s fractional operational calculus](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00549).

A very recent preprint reports a strict compact-window Weil bound strong enough for this application, but its interval certificate should be independently audited before foundational use. [Chuk](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.24827).

\Theta_\omega\text{ inner}
\iff I\pm H_{\omega,a}\succeq0

\]

parts:
The project has developed into a coherent theory of how the zero set of \(\zeta\) is encoded at three different resolutions:

1. a time-domain positivity criterion with a quantitative margin;
2. an inverse-spectral family of positive Kreĭn strings;
3. a finite-resolution theory describing when a hypothetical off-line zero becomes detectable.

It does not prove RH or a new zero-free region. But, subject to final human verification of several technical points, it appears to contain multiple substantial and potentially publishable results.

## The logical structure

| Layer | Main object | What has been established |
|---|---|---|
| [Margin paper](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/354845a0bb49/project_sources/02-psi_omega_margin-2-.pdf) | Shifted screw function \(\Psi_\omega(t)\) | Quantitative margin, sharp transition at the rightmost-zero boundary, exponential response to a violating zero, and new one-sided/integrated RH criteria |
| [Omega-string paper](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/354845a0bb49/project_sources/01-PAPER_omega_string_4-1-.pdf) | Stieltjes–Weyl function \(q_\omega\) and string \(m_\omega\) | Explicit positive spectral measure, exact link to \(\Psi_\omega\), bulk and ultraviolet laws, and an RH-equivalent continuation to \(\omega=0\) |
| [Defect-depth paper](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/354845a0bb49/project_sources/03-PAPER_defect_depth_1.pdf) | Hankel moments, Christoffel kernels, continued fractions | Exact finite-rank failure mechanism and a Green-function law for the resolution depth of an exterior spectral defect |

The starting screw-function and logarithmic-derivative positivity ideas belong to Suzuki and Lagarias. Suzuki established RH-equivalent screw-function criteria, while Lagarias proved the underlying equivalence between half-plane zero location and positivity of the logarithmic derivative. The present work’s novelty is therefore primarily quantitative, inverse-spectral, and perturbative—not the existence of a positivity reformulation itself. [Suzuki](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.03682), [Lagarias](https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa89/aa8932.pdf).

## What has been proved

### 1. The shifted criterion has an explicit margin

Writing

\[
\Theta=\sup_\rho \Re\rho,\qquad
\vartheta=\Theta-\frac12,\qquad
S_\omega=\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\left(\frac12+\omega\right),
\]

the margin paper obtains

\[
\Psi_\omega(t)
=
S_\omega t+
\left(\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\right)'\!\left(\frac12+\omega\right)
+R_\omega(t),
\]

with an explicit bound

\[
|R_\omega(t)|\leq A^*(\omega)e^{-(\omega-\vartheta)t}
\]

whenever the half-plane \(\Re\rho\leq \frac12+\omega\) is known.

Consequences include:

- Whenever the required zero-free half-plane holds, \(\Psi_\omega\) is eventually positive with a strict linear margin. In fact, positivity begins before an explicit threshold \(t_0(\omega)\leq 0.0129\,\omega\).
- The critical shift is exactly
  \[
  \omega_c=\Theta-\frac12.
  \]
  Above and at \(\omega_c\), \(\Psi_\omega(t)\) grows linearly; below it, it has two-sided exponentially growing oscillations.
- A zero at \(\Re\rho=\frac12+\delta>\frac12+\omega\) contributes an oscillation with growth rate \(e^{(\delta-\omega)t}\) and an explicit amplitude of order \(\tau^{-2}\).
- Combining verified zeros and classical zero-free regions gives rigorous but finite windows of unconditional positivity. These computations verify constants and formulas; they do not supply evidence for the infinite-tail statement needed for RH.

The paper also derives conceptually cleaner equivalent formulations:

\[
\mathrm{RH}
\iff
\int_0^\infty \Psi^-(t)\,dt<\infty,
\]

and RH is equivalent to eventual positivity after one further integration of \(\Psi\). More generally, any one-sided exponential bound on \(\Psi_\omega\) translates directly into a zero-free half-plane. This is, in my view, the most promising RH-facing result in the project: it replaces exact pointwise positivity by averaged control of only the negative part.

### 2. There is an explicit positive shifted zeta-string family

For \(\sigma=\frac12+\omega\), the omega-string paper defines

\[
q_\omega(z)=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{-z}}\,
\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\left(\sigma+\sqrt{-z}\right).
\]

It proves that \(q_\omega\) is a Stieltjes function:

- unconditionally for \(\omega\geq \frac12\);
- more generally whenever \(\Re\rho<\frac12+\omega\).

Its spectral measure is explicitly absolutely continuous. In the frequency coordinate \(u\),

\[
\rho_\omega(u)
=
\frac1\pi\sum_\rho
\frac{\sigma-\Re\rho}
{(\sigma-\Re\rho)^2+(u-\Im\rho)^2}.
\]

Thus every zero becomes a Lorentzian resonance whose width is its horizontal distance from the boundary line. Under RH, every width is exactly \(\omega\).

Several exact bridges follow:

\[
\Psi_\omega(t)
=
\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{1-\cos(ut)}{u^2}\rho_\omega(u)\,du,
\]

\[
S_\omega=\pi\rho_\omega(0),
\]

and the associated string has asymptotic bulk density

\[
\frac{m_\omega(x)}x\longrightarrow S_\omega^{-2}.
\]

At the opposite end it has the universal ultraviolet law

\[
m_\omega(x)\sim\frac{4x}{(\log x)^2}
\qquad (x\downarrow0),
\]

independent of \(\omega\) at leading order.

Finally,

\[
\mathrm{RH}
\iff
q_\omega\text{ is Stieltjes for every }\omega>0.
\]

Under RH, as \(\omega\downarrow0\), the Lorentzian spectral measure converges vaguely to Kotani’s pure-point measure, and the strings converge at continuity points. Without RH, a zero beyond the shifted boundary produces non-real poles and destroys the positive realization.

### 3. Finite spectral resolution has an exact defect-detection law

The defect-depth paper first proves abstract results independent of zeta:

- Resolvent compactification converts an unbounded Stieltjes measure into a finite measure on \([0,1]\).
- Compactified moments and Taylor coefficients of the Weyl function are related by an invertible triangular transform, degree by degree.
- Rank-one and conjugate rank-two defects perturb Hankel determinants through exact Christoffel–Darboux kernel formulas.
- The first failed Hankel positivity condition determines exactly the first nonpositive coefficient in the Stieltjes continued fraction—and hence the first anomalous mass or gap of the corresponding string.

For a fixed exterior defect of strength \(\varepsilon\),

\[
\frac{n_\varepsilon}{\log(1/\varepsilon)}
\longrightarrow
\frac{1}{2g(c)},
\]

where \(g(c)\) is the Green distance of the defect from the admissible support.

For the shifted zeta system, a hypothetical quartet with horizontal excess

\[
\eta=\delta-\omega>0
\]

becomes a conjugate rank-two defect. The same \(\eta\) controls both representations:

- time domain: exponential growth \(e^{\eta t}\);
- inverse-spectral domain: Christoffel/Hankel detection depth controlled by \(g(c)\).

The time-domain first-detection scale is rigorously

\[
\eta t_{\mathrm{first}}
=
2\log\tau+\log\log\tau+\log(S_\omega/\eta)+o(1),
\]

under the stated transversality assumptions. The predicted high-height inverse-spectral depth is polynomially larger, roughly

\[
n\asymp
\frac{\tau^2\log\tau}{\eta\sqrt{s_0}},
\]

but this moving-point law remains conjectural/numerically supported rather than proved.

## Interpretations

The cleanest interpretation is that \(\omega\) is a resolution or broadening scale. At positive \(\omega\), the zero set is Poisson-smoothed into an absolutely continuous density. Sending \(\omega\to0\) attempts to deconvolve that density into the discrete zero spectrum. RH says precisely that this entire deconvolution path remains inside the cone of positive/passive Stieltjes systems.

There is also a legitimate critical-phenomena analogy. Under RH,

\[
S_\omega\sim B(0)\omega,
\qquad
\rho_\infty(\omega)=S_\omega^{-2}\sim \frac{1}{B(0)^2\omega^2}.
\]

Thus the margin vanishes linearly while the string’s bulk density diverges quadratically. Calling this a “critical softening” or “infinite-inertia endpoint” is defensible. Calling it localization would be too strong because no eigenfunction or dynamical localization theorem has been established.

The defect paper supplies another interpretation: continued-fraction depth is a geometric distance-to-positivity coordinate. The Green function measures how many moments, Taylor coefficients, or string beads must be resolved before an inadmissible spectral feature becomes visible. That idea should have applications beyond zeta—in moment problems, inverse spectral theory, and Christoffel-function anomaly detection.

Perhaps the most important negative interpretation is also useful: the inverse-spectral coordinate is much worse conditioned than the time-domain coordinate for detecting high zeros. The string picture is structurally illuminating, but it does not appear to amplify off-line defects into an easier computational test.

## Highest-priority paths forward

1. **Complete the proof audit.** The three places I would scrutinize most carefully are:

   - the normalization and endpoint conventions in the Kasahara Tauberian arguments;
   - the Landau-theorem hypotheses in the integrated and negative-part criteria;
   - the claim in Lemma 5.2 that the signed cut correction changes the first rank-two threshold by only \(O(1)\). Quadratic-form comparability controls the Hermitian Christoffel kernel, but stability of the small rank-two negative channel may require a stronger quantitative nondegeneracy argument. The ratio-limit result is likely more robust than the stated \(O(1)\) conclusion.

2. **Prove rank-two nondegeneracy for the actual compactified zeta density.** The main defect theorem presently assumes it. Strong orthogonal-polynomial asymptotics on \([0,1]\) should make the negative channel explicit and would simultaneously support the moving-point analysis.

3. **Establish the double-scaling Christoffel theorem.** The mathematically richest open problem is the joint limit in which the defect approaches the endpoint while the required degree tends to infinity. This should explain the observed crossover between the continuous-interval regime and the quasi-discrete regime governed by local zero spacing.

4. **Develop a multi-defect theorem.** An actual RH failure need not be one quartet. The finite-rank determinant formula already extends to \(r\) defects. One could prove conditional theorems for finitely many extremal quartets, tied horizontal rates, or a separated rightmost cluster. That would turn the present model into a more faithful conditional description of an actual failure.

5. **Study the critical string at \(\omega_c\).** If \(\Theta\) is attained, the critical measure contains point masses from the extremal zeros embedded in an absolutely continuous background; if it is not attained, it does not. Characterizing this distinction intrinsically on the string side could be quite interesting.

6. **For an RH-oriented program, concentrate on one-sided averaged control.** The concrete target is:

   \[
   \int_0^T\Psi_\omega^-(t)\,dt
   \leq C e^{\varepsilon T}
   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
   \Theta\leq\frac12+\omega+\varepsilon.
   \]

   It would suffice to prove such bounds for a sequence \(\omega_j,\varepsilon_j\to0\). This creates a potentially more flexible “approach the endpoint through approximate one-sided estimates” program. Zero-density estimates alone cannot achieve it because they permit a single violating zero, but variational explicit-formula methods, reproducing kernels, or arithmetic averaging may interact better with the negative-part formulation.

7. **Extend to \(L\)-function families.** Suzuki’s extended Selberg-class work confirms that screw-function structures persist more broadly, with additional complications from real zeros. Averaging over characters could produce genuinely unconditional positivity statements that are unavailable for a single \(L\)-function. [Suzuki’s Selberg-class extension](https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.12832v2).

My overall assessment is that the omega-string construction is the conceptual centerpiece, the margin paper contains the most direct analytic-number-theory results, and the defect-depth theory may be the strongest standalone mathematical artifact. The program has not made RH materially easier, but it has produced a surprisingly unified and quantitative account of how RH failure would manifest across time-domain, spectral, moment, and continued-fraction representations.

I think the idea is mathematically legitimate and potentially striking, but the useful statement would be narrower than “RH follows from AdS/CFT.” It would be:

> If the shifted zeta response can be realized as the boundary response of an independently positive bulk theory for arbitrarily small \(\omega>0\), then RH follows.

That is already a precise conditional theorem suggested by the omega-string results. The challenge is ensuring that the bulk positivity is genuinely independent rather than merely reconstructed from the desired boundary positivity.

## A precise holographic RH theorem

Set

\[
G_\omega(p^2):=q_\omega(-p^2)
=
\frac{1}{p}\frac{\xi'}{\xi}\left(\frac12+\omega+p\right).
\]

Suppose there is a sequence \(\omega_n\downarrow0\) such that \(G_{\omega_n}\) is the Euclidean two-point function of a translation-invariant, reflection-positive Hermitian boundary operator, with the usual spectral condition. Its Källén–Lehmann representation would then have the form

\[
G_{\omega_n}(p^2)
=
\int_0^\infty
\frac{d\mu_n(\lambda)}{\lambda+p^2},
\qquad d\mu_n\geq0.
\]

Equivalently, \(q_{\omega_n}\) is Stieltjes. But the omega-string theorem says that an off-critical zero with \(\beta>\frac12\) creates non-real poles in every \(q_\omega\) with

\[
0<\omega<\beta-\frac12.
\]

Since \(\omega_n\to0\), such a zero would eventually contradict reflection positivity. The functional equation supplies the corresponding right-half-plane zero if the original one lies to the left. Therefore:

\[
\boxed{
\text{Reflection-positive realizations of }q_{\omega_n}
\text{ for some }\omega_n\downarrow0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm{RH}.
}
\]

The bulk version is equally clean: if \(q_{\omega_n}\) is the Dirichlet-to-Neumann or Weyl response of a nonnegative self-adjoint bulk operator, then it has a positive Stieltjes spectral representation, and the same argument proves RH.

One does not need to prove full AdS/CFT. A rigorous special-case bulk/boundary dictionary at the level of two-point functions would suffice.

## The modular-surface connection is real—but currently insufficient

Define the scattering-type function

\[
\Theta_\omega(z)
=
\frac{\xi(\frac12-\omega-iz)}
     {\xi(\frac12+\omega-iz)}
=
\frac{\xi(\frac12+\omega+iz)}
     {\xi(\frac12+\omega-iz)}.
\]

For real \(u\),

\[
\rho_\omega(u)
=
\frac{1}{2\pi i}\frac{d}{du}\log \Theta_\omega(u).
\]

Thus the spectral density of the \(\omega\)-string is literally the derivative of a scattering phase—a Wigner–Smith time-delay density.

At \(\omega=\frac12\),

\[
\Theta_{1/2}(z)
=
\frac{\xi(1+iz)}{\xi(1-iz)},
\]

which is, up to convention-dependent elementary factors, the scattering coefficient of the modular surface evaluated at \(s=(1-iz)/2\). The standard modular scattering coefficient can be written

\[
\phi(s)=\frac{\xi(2-2s)}{\xi(2s)}.
\]

The corresponding scattering poles are half the zeta zeros; RH says that the nontrivial ones lie on \(\Re s=\frac14\). This exact automorphic scattering relation is well established. [Petridis–Raulf–Risager](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1111.6615).

This is a compelling endpoint dictionary:

\[
\text{modular bulk scattering}
\longleftrightarrow
\Theta_{1/2}
\longrightarrow
\rho_{1/2}
\longrightarrow
q_{1/2}
\longrightarrow
\text{positive Kreĭn string}.
\]

However, the modular Laplacian is already self-adjoint and its scattering matrix is unitary on the physical line unconditionally. Ordinary scattering unitarity does not force its resonances onto \(\Re s=\frac14\). Consequently:

| Bulk property | Boundary consequence | Enough for RH? |
|---|---|---:|
| Unitarity on the physical scattering line | \(|\Theta_\omega(u)|=1\) for real \(u\) | No |
| Positive scattering-phase derivative | \(\rho_\omega(u)\geq0\) on the cut | Still not by itself |
| Causal/passive analytic response | \(q_\omega\) Herglotz/Stieltjes | Yes |
| Reflection-positive boundary two-point function | Positive Källén–Lehmann measure | Yes |
| Nonnegative self-adjoint bulk Weyl problem | Stieltjes Dirichlet-to-Neumann map | Yes |

The distinction between the second and third rows matters: below the critical shift, the boundary density can conceivably remain positive while \(q_\omega\) acquires additional non-real pole terms. Pointwise positivity of the time delay is weaker than full analytic passivity.

## What would count as genuinely new information?

The current Kreĭn string already provides an exact “toy holographic” realization:

\[
\text{boundary }q_\omega
\longleftrightarrow
\text{one-dimensional bulk string }m_\omega.
\]

But constructing the string from \(q_\omega\) does not independently prove positivity. The positive string exists precisely when the boundary function is Stieltjes. Using that construction to establish RH would therefore be circular.

To gain leverage, the bulk must arise from an independent principle—for example:

- a fixed positive local action;
- a nonnegative self-adjoint elliptic operator on a specified geometry;
- reflection positivity inherited from conventional bulk quantization;
- an Einstein/dilaton equation whose solutions automatically have positive radial measure;
- a causal passive scattering system known independently of \(\xi\).

Reflection positivity can indeed pass from a conventionally quantized AdS field to its boundary restriction, while scattering operators on asymptotically hyperbolic Einstein manifolds encode conformal boundary operators. These are genuine mathematical aspects of the AdS/CFT dictionary. [Rehren](https://arxiv.org/pdf/hep-th/0411086), [Graham–Zworski](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0109089).

The missing task is to identify that independently positive bulk response with the particular arithmetic function \(q_\omega\).

## The most plausible bulk interpretation

The current strings do not look like ordinary pure AdS radial problems. Their ultraviolet behavior is

\[
m_\omega(x)\sim\frac{4x}{(\log x)^2},
\]

which contains logarithmic running rather than the pure power-law behavior expected from an undeformed CFT. Meanwhile, their infrared bulk is homogeneous:

\[
m_\omega(x)\sim S_\omega^{-2}x.
\]

I would therefore expect the appropriate interpretation, if one exists, to be one of:

- an asymptotically AdS theory with a running scalar or dilaton;
- a holographic RG flow rather than a fixed CFT;
- a defect or generalized-free boundary theory;
- a radial reduction of an automorphic scattering problem;
- a finite-temperature or dissipative family in which \(\omega\) acts as a broadening scale.

Under RH, positive \(\omega\) turns the discrete zero spectrum into Lorentzians of width \(\omega\), while \(\omega\downarrow0\) produces stable pure-point modes. Physically, this resembles a dissipative or horizon-like system approaching a horizonless discrete-spectrum limit. The diverging bulk density,

\[
\rho_\infty(\omega)\sim\frac{1}{B(0)^2\omega^2},
\]

could correspond to an increasingly long or heavy infrared throat. These are suggestive interpretations, not yet mathematical identifications.

## A concrete research program

I would pursue this in four stages.

1. **Prove the abstract holographic implication.**

   Formalize the theorem relating reflection positivity, the Källén–Lehmann representation, the Stieltjes property of \(q_\omega\), and RH. Include the stronger observation that a sequence \(\omega_n\downarrow0\) suffices.

2. **Complete the modular endpoint dictionary.**

   Derive carefully:

   \[
   \Theta_{1/2}\leftrightarrow\phi_{\mathrm{modular}},
   \qquad
   \rho_{1/2}=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\partial_u\log\phi,
   \]

   and determine whether \(q_{1/2}\) is best understood as a resolvent, impedance, time-delay transform, or derivative of a scattering determinant.

3. **Search for a common bulk realizing general \(\omega\).**

   The decisive question is whether the \(m_\omega\) are separate engineered strings or radial slices/boundary conditions of a single bulk system. Suzuki’s shift-composition law may provide an RG-like semigroup, but compatibility with genuine radial Hamilton–Jacobi evolution must be proved.

   Automorphic deformations, Robin walls, dilaton backgrounds, and inverse asymptotically-hyperbolic problems are natural places to look.

4. **Establish an early no-go criterion.**

   Test whether \(q_\omega\) can be a conventional CFT two-point function. Its non-power-law momentum dependence suggests not. If ordinary conformal invariance rules it out, the correct target should be stated as holographic QFT, defect CFT, or automorphic holography rather than standard AdS/CFT.

My assessment is that a result entitled something like “The Riemann hypothesis as holographic reflection positivity” is achievable at the level of a rigorous equivalence or conditional theorem. Actually proving RH this way would require the much deeper step of finding an independently unitary bulk realization for arbitrarily small \(\omega\). That is unlikely—but it is a sharply formulated, non-vacuous research question, and the exact modular-surface endpoint makes it considerably more than a loose analogy.

The project now has three logically distinct levels.

## 1. Boundary reflection positivity is exactly related to RH

For each shift \(\omega>0\), define

\[
\Theta_\omega(u)
=
\frac{\xi(\frac12-\omega-iu)}
     {\xi(\frac12+\omega-iu)}
\]

and

\[
q_\omega(z)
=
\frac{1}{\sqrt{-z}}
\frac{\xi'}{\xi}
\left(\frac12+\omega+\sqrt{-z}\right).
\]

The following chain is essentially exact:

\[
\Theta_\omega\text{ is inner}
\Longleftrightarrow
\Re\rho\leq\frac12+\omega
\Longleftrightarrow
q_\omega\text{ is Stieltjes}.
\]

A Stieltjes representation

\[
q_\omega(z)
=
\int_0^\infty\frac{d\sigma_\omega(\lambda)}{\lambda-z},
\qquad d\sigma_\omega\geq0,
\]

makes

\[
\widetilde C_\omega(p)=q_\omega(-|p|^2)
=
\int_0^\infty
\frac{d\sigma_\omega(\lambda)}
{|p|^2+\lambda}
\]

a Källén–Lehmann covariance. Therefore it defines an Osterwalder–Schrader reflection-positive generalized free field.

Consequently,

\[
\boxed{
\mathrm{RH}
\Longleftrightarrow
C_{\omega_n}\text{ is reflection positive for some }
\omega_n\downarrow0.
}
\]

So RH really is equivalent to reflection positivity of a family of boundary theories approaching the critical shift.

This part is already an exact reformulation. Its limitation is that the positive boundary field is reconstructed from \(q_\omega\) only after the relevant zero-free half-plane is known. It does not independently explain why positivity holds.

## 2. The holographic idea is to derive that boundary positivity from a positive bulk

The desired direction is:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Prime-gamma bulk"] --> B["Causal positive radial evolution"]
    B --> C["Boundary transfer Θω"]
    C --> D["Positive boundary kernel"]
    D --> E["Stieltjes covariance and OS positivity"]
    E --> F["Zero-free half-plane"]
```

For shifts \(\omega_n\downarrow0\), the last step would imply RH.

The important word is **independently**. The bulk must be specified directly from gamma factors and primes, and its positive energy must be proved without first assuming that \(q_\omega\) is Stieltjes or that \(\Theta_\omega\) is inner.

Otherwise one has merely taken the desired boundary positivity and reconstructed a bulk from it.

## 3. Suzuki’s arithmetic canonical system is the candidate bulk

Suzuki constructs a prime-side Hankel kernel whose boundary scattering function is \(\Theta_\omega\). In logarithmic radial coordinates,

\[
k_\omega(t)
=
\sum_{n\geq1}
\frac{c_\omega(n)}{\sqrt n}\,
\kappa_\omega(t-\log n).
\]

This has a very suggestive holographic structure:

- \(t\) is a radial or scale coordinate;
- \(\kappa_\omega\) is the universal archimedean propagation kernel;
- arithmetic information enters as delayed layers at depths \(\log n\);
- the boundary transfer function is \(\Theta_\omega\);
- global causal contractivity is equivalent to the shifted zero-free condition.

The reflected finite-volume operator has kernel depending on \(r+s\), rather than \(r-s\). Its two reflection channels are

\[
I+H_{\omega,L},
\qquad
I-H_{\omega,L}.
\]

Thus

\[
I\pm H_{\omega,L}\succeq0
\]

is a literal radial reflection-positivity condition. Equivalently, after reflecting one radial coordinate,

\[
H_{\omega,L}=V_{\omega,L}R_L,
\]

this becomes finite-horizon passivity:

\[
I-V_{\omega,L}^{*}V_{\omega,L}\succeq0.
\]

The causal Gram/Riccati factor

\[
I-V_{\omega,L}^{*}V_{\omega,L}
=
G_{\omega,L}^{*}G_{\omega,L}
\]

is the positive bulk-energy decomposition. This is the technical heart of the holographic interpretation.

## 4. What the first-slab result establishes

The arithmetic layers enter at depths

\[
\log2,\ \log3,\ \log4,\ldots.
\]

Before \(L=\log2\), only the \(n=1\) gamma layer exists. This is the **prime-free first slab**.

What we have now established is:

\[
I\pm H_{\omega,L}\succ0
\qquad
\left(
10^{-6}\leq\omega\leq\frac14,\;
L\leq\log2
\right),
\]

together with:

- qualitative positivity for all sufficiently small \(\omega>0\);
- unconditional positivity at \(\omega=\tfrac12\) and in a neighborhood below it;
- existence of the infinite-dimensional causal Sonine/Riccati factor;
- strong convergence of its finite modal approximants.

This is significant because its positivity was obtained directly from the archimedean kernel and the prime-free Weil form—not by assuming RH or reconstructing a string from an already-positive measure.

In holographic language, we have constructed and controlled the first radial segment of an independently positive bulk.

## 5. Why this does not yet imply RH

RH requires positivity of the complete bulk at every radial depth, along shifts tending to zero:

\[
\mathrm{RH}
\Longleftrightarrow
I\pm H_{\omega_n,L}\succeq0
\quad
\text{for all }L>0
\text{ and some }\omega_n\downarrow0.
\]

We have proved it only for

\[
L\leq\log2.
\]

The first slab contains no primes. It therefore cannot exclude an off-critical zero, because the global zero structure is encoded in the cumulative effect of all arithmetic layers.

The remaining conceptual program is:

\[
\text{positive gamma slab}
\longrightarrow
\text{add the }n=2\text{ layer}
\longrightarrow
\text{add }n=3
\longrightarrow\cdots
\longrightarrow
\text{global positive bulk}.
\]

If positivity could be propagated through all layers for a sequence \(\omega_n\downarrow0\), that would prove RH.

## 6. Where the modular surface fits

At the unconditional endpoint,

\[
\Theta_{1/2}(u)
=
\frac{u-i}{u+i}\,
\varphi\left(\frac{1-iu}{2}\right),
\]

where \(\varphi\) is the modular-surface cusp scattering coefficient.

So at \(\omega=\tfrac12\), the boundary amplitude genuinely comes from a known positive geometric bulk—the modular Laplacian—plus one elementary completion channel.

But ordinary modular scattering unitarity is insufficient for RH. It gives unit modulus on the physical line, whereas RH requires upper-half-plane analyticity and contractivity as the shift approaches zero. Suzuki’s canonical system is attractive because it turns that missing property into causal bulk positivity.

## 7. The three “bulks” should not be conflated

| Construction | What it gives | Can it prove positivity independently? |
|---|---|---:|
| Krein string reconstructed from \(q_\omega\) | Exact positive inverse-spectral realization | No; positivity is assumed through the Stieltjes property |
| Modular surface at \(\omega=\tfrac12\) | Independently positive geometric scattering bulk | Yes, but only at the unconditional endpoint |
| Suzuki prime-gamma canonical system | Candidate causal bulk for all shifts | Potentially; first slab now established |

My assessment is that the project has become more concretely holographic, not less. Initially, “holographic reflection positivity” was primarily an exact dictionary. The first-slab work supplies the beginning of an actual non-circular mechanism: a directly specified radial bulk, a causal energy factorization, and a reflected boundary kernel.

What remains is precisely the difficult arithmetic part: showing that positivity survives as the prime layers enter. That is where the route either becomes a genuine approach to RH or stops at a strong local canonical-system theorem.
